_README: HAND RESOLUTIONS FOR CALL SITES THE AST CANNOT NAME.
edge_function_writes.mjs classifies every .from()/.rpc() site and refuses to publish a map with
any site it cannot resolve. That refusal is the point: an extractor that folds 'cannot tell' into
'writes nothing' will eventually clear a real kernel bypass. This file is where a human resolves
the remainder, with the evidence that justifies each answer.
tables: [...]  the computed name comes from a literal map in the same file, and these are all
the values it can take. Enumerated by reading that map, quoted in `evidence`.
unbounded:true the target comes from a database row or caller input, so it can be ANY routine
or table. This is a PERMANENT answer, not a to-do. A source with an unbounded
write site can never be CLEARED by the write map — the safe direction — because
the honest statement is 'this may write anything'.
Every entry is keyed by function:line and is checked on each run: if the site moves or vanishes,
the entry is stale and the check fails rather than silently covering nothing.

sites.evidence: tgt comes from the literal target map at kb_embed/index.ts:79-81 — kb_chunks: { table: 'kb_chunks', ... } and company_faq: { table: 'company_faq', ... }. No other key exists in that map.
cfg = CONTENT[b.type], and CONTENT is a literal Record in os_ops/index.ts whose members name exactly these five tables. An unknown type returns 400 unknown_content_type before the write.
w = EDITABLE[b.entity], a literal Record in os_ops/index.ts naming exactly these nine tables. An entity outside it returns 400 field_not_editable before the write.
name is a caller-supplied routine identifier. The gateway can invoke any routine the service role may execute, so its write set is not statically bounded.
same shape as ai_gateway: the routine name arrives with the request rather than from a literal map.

ex is a row read from the executor queue, so ex.target is whatever a queued row names. This is the executor dispatcher: being able to call any registered routine is its purpose, and no static bound exists.
d.health_fn is a column on the department row, so the routine is chosen by data rather than by code.
cfg.rpc comes from an agent configuration rather than a literal in this file.

WS maps a workspace action to a fn_ws_* reader. Those are read-only workspace projections today, but the mapping is indexed by caller-supplied `action` and the set is maintained elsewhere, so it is recorded unbounded rather than enumerated from a map that may grow without this file noticing.
